stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In 1950, about one in three workers at the Harlow textile mill belonged to a union. By 1990, that share had fallen to one in ten. ______ in 1925, before any union organizers had reached the town, not a single worker at the mill had been a member.
explanation: Write down the year in each sentence: 1950, 1990, then 1925. The blank sentence goes back to before the first date, so it needs a word that points backward in time. 'Earlier' does that. Being able to place each sentence on a timeline is what you need for every Timeline and steps transition question on the test, because the trap there is assuming the passage only moves forward.

B.why: You assumed the passage keeps moving forward because the sentence comes last. Compare the dates: 1925 is before 1950 and 1990, so 'Later' points the wrong way.

C.why: You chose a cause word, but a drop in membership by 1990 cannot cause something that happened in 1925. The sentences are linked by time, not by cause.

D.why: You read the last sentence as an illustration of the earlier ones. It doesn't give a sample of the 1950 or 1990 figures. It describes a different and earlier point in time.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: According to her notebooks, the composer Clara Ostrowski wrote her 1912 string quartet in three stages. First, she sketched the main melodies at the piano. Then she wrote out a separate part for each of the four instruments. ______ she revised the entire score after hearing the players rehearse it.
explanation: The passage says there are three stages and marks them for you: 'First', 'Then', and the blank. The blank sentence is the third and last stage, so you need a word that closes a sequence. 'Finally' does that. Finding the count and the step words is the first move on any process passage in a Timeline and steps transition question.

B.why: 'Previously' sends the reader back to before the earlier steps. Revising after rehearsal is the last of the three stages, not something that came before the sketching.

C.why: You treated the third stage as one more step of the same kind. 'Similarly' signals a likeness between two things, but this sentence moves the process forward to its end. It doesn't compare revising with copying out parts.

D.why: You picked a cause word because one step came after another. Writing out the parts did not cause the revision. The passage only says the revision happened third.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Around 1650, many European maps of North America showed California as a large island, separated from the mainland by a long, narrow sea. ______ explorers who traveled overland around the head of that sea reported that California was joined to the continent, and mapmakers redrew the coastline to match.
explanation: The first sentence describes how maps looked around 1650. The second sentence describes what changed after explorers corrected that view, and mapmakers can only redraw a map after it exists. The blank therefore moves forward in time, and 'Later' is the word for that. Telling which way a sentence moves in time is the core skill behind Timeline and steps transition questions.

B.why: 'Earlier' would put the correction before the mistaken maps. That can't be right, because the coastline had to be drawn wrong before it could be redrawn.

C.why: The second sentence isn't one case of maps showing California as an island. It reports the discovery that overturned those maps, so it's a later event, not an example.

D.why: 'Similarly' signals that the second sentence matches the first. It doesn't match. It reverses the island idea at a later date.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In 2024, volunteers on a beach in Costa Rica recorded a green sea turtle as it dug a nest in the sand. A metal tag on its front flipper showed that the turtle was not new to that beach. ______ in 2004, researchers had attached that same tag when the turtle came ashore to lay its first nest there.
explanation: The first sentence is set in 2024, and the blank sentence is set in 2004. The blank sentence goes back twenty years to explain where the tag came from, so it needs a word that points backward. 'Previously' does that. On the test, a sentence that steps back to give background is the most common place the Timeline and steps trap is set.

B.why: This is the subtype's main trap. You assumed the passage moves forward because the sentence comes after the others. 'Subsequently' means 'after that', but 2004 is before 2024.

C.why: You chose a cause word, but the 2024 nest did not cause a tag to be fitted in 2004. Events cannot cause things that happened before them.

D.why: 'In addition' treats the last sentence as one more fact on the same level. It's actually a jump back in time that explains the tag. The time relationship is the point, and this choice ignores it.
